title: Impact of NAFTA Tariff Removal on Bilateral Trade Flows

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Difference-in-Differences (DID)

Rationale  
• Treatment varies across country-pairs (NAFTA members vs. non-members) and across time (pre- vs. post-NAFTA).  
• DID compares the change in log bilateral trade for treated pairs to the concurrent change for control pairs, purging common shocks and permanent pair-specific factors with two-way fixed effects.

Key assumptions  
1. Parallel trends: absent tariff removal, the treated and control pairs would have experienced the same trend in trade flows.  
2. SUTVA/no spillovers: treatment of NAFTA pairs does not directly affect control pairs’ trade.  
3. Stable composition: no differential entry/exit of country pairs correlated with treatment.

## 2. R Code
```r
############################################################
# Impact of NAFTA tariff removal on bilateral trade flows
# ---------------------------------------------------------
# Requires packages: data.table, fixest, ggplot2
############################################################
library(data.table)
library(fixest)
library(ggplot2)

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
data_path <- "experiments/exp_b/data/s44_data.csv"
dt <- fread(data_path)

# 2. Baseline DID with two-way fixed effects -------------------------------
did_main <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  data = dt,
                  cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n==== Baseline DID result ====\n")
print(coeftable(did_main, se = "cluster"))

# 3. Robustness check 1: placebo (pre-period only) -------------------------
placebo <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                 data = dt[post == 0],          # only pre-NAFTA observations
                 cluster = ~unit_id)

cat("\n==== Placebo DID (pre-period) ====\n")
print(coeftable(placebo, se = "cluster"))

# 4. Robustness check 2: two-way clustered SE ------------------------------
did_twoc <- feols(y ~ treat_x_post | unit_id + period,
                  data   = dt,
                  cluster = ~unit_id + period)

cat("\n==== Baseline DID with two-way clustering ====\n")
print(coeftable(did_twoc, se = "twoway"))

# 5. Robustness check 3: event-study (dynamic effects) ---------------------
# Construct relative time to treatment
# Assume first post period = 0, so leads are negative
dt[, rel_time := ifelse(treated == 1, period - min(period[post == 1]),  # treated pairs
                        period - min(period[post == 1]))]               # control pairs for balance

# Keep -3 … +3 windows and omit -1 as reference
dt_es <- dt[rel_time >= -3 & rel_time <= 3]
dt_es[, rel_time_f := factor(rel_time)]
event_mod <- feols(y ~ i(rel_time_f, treated, ref = -1) | unit_id + period,
                   data = dt_es,
                   cluster = ~unit_id)

# Plot event-study coefficients
es_plot <- coefplot(event_mod, main = "Event-study: NAFTA and Trade",
                    xlab = "Years relative to tariff removal",
                    ylab = "Log-trade effect")
ggsave("event_study.png", es_plot, width = 6, height = 4)

# 6. Output a concise summary ----------------------------------------------
did_coef  <- coef(did_main)["treat_x_post"]
did_se    <- se(did_main, "cluster")["treat_x_post"]
did_ci    <- confint(did_main)["treat_x_post",]

cat("\n==== Summary ====\n",
    "DID point estimate (log points): ", round(did_coef, 3), "\n",
    "Robust SE: ", round(did_se, 3), "\n",
    "95% CI: [", round(did_ci[1], 3), ", ", round(did_ci[2], 3), "]\n")
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Economic intuition and prior studies suggest tariff elimination boosts trade substantially. In logarithmic terms, a 20–40 % increase translates to a coefficient of roughly +0.18 – +0.34.  
Therefore, I anticipate:  
• Positive and significant DID coefficient (≈ +0.25 log points).  
• Placebo estimate close to zero, supporting the parallel-trends assumption.  
• Event-study plot showing flat pre-trends and a discrete upward jump starting in the first post-NAFTA year.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Comparing trade flows before and after NAFTA for treated and control pairs.
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: The tariff removal under NAFTA led to a significant increase in bilateral trade flows.
